title: Kestrel and the Ledger
premise: Estate lawyer Lior Sandoval is summoned to probate a will for a dead woman she never represented—a will written in her own handwriting, which she has no memory of drafting. The document references a coded ledger that implicates the city's most powerful families in a decades-old cover-up, and when a witness to the will is found murdered wearing Lior's stolen clothes, Lior becomes both suspect and investigator. As the trial approaches, she uncovers that her missing memories were deliberately taken, and that the ledger's cipher key is hidden in the will itself. In the end, Lior chooses justice over self-preservation, entering the decoded ledger into evidence at trial and exposing the conspiracy—at the cost of her reputation, her firm, and the comfortable invisibility she once treasured.
about_author: Ulyana Voss is the pen name of a former court clerk who spent eleven years watching secrets move through probate files before writing them into fiction. She lives near a coastal archive town and claims her best plot ideas arrive during inventory season.

chapters.title: The Will That Wasn't Filed
chapters.summary: Lior Sandoval, POV. A courier delivers a will for probate—signed by Lior's own hand, dated three years ago, for a client she cannot recall. Her meticulous records show no such case. The emotional beat is quiet dread: the first crack in her identity as someone whose memory and paper trail are flawless.

chapters.title: Clothes on a Stranger
chapters.summary: Lior, POV. The will's named witness is found dead in the harbor district, dressed in garments stolen from Lior's own closet. Police treat Lior as a person of interest; her alibi is a three-day gap she can't explain. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve—she must investigate what the police won't.

chapters.title: Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Lior, POV, with an interlude from Detective Amara Reyes. Examining the will under raking light, Lior finds marginal notations forming a numeric pattern—an index, not decoration. She realizes the 'ledger' is encoded across multiple documents she may have drafted while memory-blacked. Beat: obsessive focus replacing panic.

chapters.title: The Hollow Days
chapters.summary: Lior, POV. Flashbacks reconstructed from receipts, transit logs, and a hotel keycard trace her missing seventy-two hours to the Ashgrove estate, home of the Vane family—beneficiaries contesting the will. Someone drugged her and used her legal skill as a weapon. Beat: violation and cold anger.

chapters.title: What the Witness Knew
chapters.summary: Amara Reyes, POV. The detective works the murder off-book, suspicious that evidence against Lior arrived too neatly. The victim's phone holds one deleted call—to the Vanes' fixer. Beat: reluctant alliance forming; Amara begins doubting the official narrative she's paid to uphold.

chapters.title: Cipher of Debts
chapters.summary: Lior, POV. Decoding accelerates: the ledger tracks payments laundering a wrongful death settlement from twenty years ago, signed off by a judge now presiding over her case. A threatening note appears inside her apartment—someone is close. Beat: rising paranoia, stakes made personal.

chapters.title: Trial by Ambush
chapters.summary: Lior, POV. The pretrial hearing goes badly; the prosecution produces a forged confession in her handwriting style. Her firm suspends her. She realizes the conspirators don't just want the will quashed—they want her discredited as its author. Beat: rock bottom, isolation complete.

chapters.title: The Second Hand
chapters.summary: Amara, POV. Amara finds the real killer's mistake: the stolen clothes were taken during the same window Lior was drugged—the killer had access to both. Confronting the fixer, she's nearly silenced herself but secures a recording. Beat: courage at cost; the alliance becomes open conspiracy between two women outside the law.

chapters.title: Opening Statement
chapters.summary: Lior, POV. Trial day. Instead of defending herself, Lior takes the stand as author of the will, decodes the ledger aloud, and enters it into evidence with Amara's recording attached. The courtroom erupts; the judge recuses himself mid-proceeding. Beat: climax—Lior burns her career to force truth into daylight.

chapters.title: Kestrel
chapters.summary: Lior, POV, epilogue months later. Disbarred but vindicated publicly, Lior works as an advocate for victims erased by legal machinery, keeping the ledger's final unexplained page framed on her wall—a reminder of the client she never met who planned all this before dying. Beat: bittersweet resolution; justice achieved outside the law, identity rebuilt around purpose rather than invisibility.
